texts.preamble: Santosh Kumar vs M/S R R Constructions on 27 February, 2021 In The Court Of Shri Anuj Agrawal, Additional Sessions Judge5, South East District, Saket Courts, New Delhi Revision Petition No. 289 of 2018 In The Matter Of: Santosh Kumar E3494, Gali No.81, Molarband Extn. Near Harihardev Public School, New Delhi110044 . . . . Revisionist Versus 1. M/s R R Constructions Sole Proprietorship Concern G828, Dheeraj Nagar Extension, Opposite Sector 3031, Faridabad 121003 Also at E339, Dheeraj Nagar, Faridabad, Haryana - 121003 2. Mr Lal Babu Jha, G828, Dheeraj Nagar Extension, Opposite Sector 3031, Faridabad 121003 Also at E339, Dheeraj Nagar, . . . . Respondents Instituted on : 20.04.2018 Reserved on : Not Reserved Pronounced on : 27.02.2021 Crl Rev No.289/2018 Santosh Kumar Vs. M/s R R Constructions & Anr Page No. Digitally signed by Anuj Anuj Agrawal Agrawal Date: 2021.02.27 14:56:18 +0530 Judgment
texts.facts: Thereafter, the matter got listed on several dates and none was present on behalf of revisionist/complainant on as many as three Crl Rev No.289/2018 Santosh Kumar Vs. 4. The revisionist has raised number of grounds impugning the order dated 08.02.2018. However, before dealing with the said grounds, the question of maintainability of the instant revision petition is to be decided. 5. In the instant case the complaint alleging offences punishable under Section 16 (1) (1A) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act and the Rules is filed by complainant Shri Amit Kumar Singh, Director, M/s Trending Flooring Private Ltd. The complainant can challenge the order of acquittal by filing an application for special leave to appeal in the Delhi High Court and not in the Sessions Court. Preliminary objection regarding maintainability of the appeal before the Sessions Court was rejected. That order was challenged before this Court (Delhi High Court) and it was held that Sessions Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the appeal. He cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court.
texts.arguments: Ld counsel for revisionist has vehemently argued that present revision petition is very much maintainable in law as the impugned order is not 'interlocutory' in nature. Per contra, Ld Counsel for respondent has argued for dismissal of instant revision petition on the ground of maintainablity arguing that only an appeal before Hon'ble High Court in terms of statutory provisions of section 378(4) Cr.PC. should have been filed as the impugned order has resulted into acquittal of accused. 7. Before deciding the question of maintainability, the relevant statutory provisions are being reproduced for the sake of convenience : "Section 256 in The Code Of Criminal Procedure, 1973 256. Non appearance or death of complainant. I am fortified in my view by dicta of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subhash Chand Vs State (Delhi Administration), 2013 (1) JCC 338, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court in para no.s 17 and 21 held as under: "17. Sub Section (4) of Section 378 makes provision for appeal against an order of acquittal passed in case instituted upon complaint. Further, Hon'ble Delhi High Court in a recent judgment of "The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. Vs. Sushil Kumar", Crl. Appeal No. 972/2014, decided on 3.9.2014, at para no. 10 to 18 held as under: "10. 14. The controversy now is no longer res integra in view of the pronouncement of law by Supreme Court in 'Subhash Chand Vs. State (Delhi Administration)', (2013) 2 SCC 17. It was a complaint case under Section 7 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, in which Subhash Chand was tried and he was acquitted by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate. Section 378 (4) places no restriction on the complainant... ... ..." 16. In a recent case 'Bhavuben Dineshbhai Makwana Vs. State of Gujarat & Others', 2013 Crl LJ 4225, Full Bench of Gujarat High Court answering the reference on question number (3) 'If the victim prefers an appeal before this Court, challenging the acquittal, invoking his right under proviso to section 372 of CrPC, whether that appellant is required to first seek leave of the Court, Crl Rev No.289/2018 Santosh Kumar Vs. M/s R R Constructions & Anr Page No. 9 of 11 ANUJ ANUJ AGRAWAL AGRAWAL Date: 2021.02.27 14:57:36 +0530 as is required in case of appeal being preferred by the State? ', held: 'If the victim also happens to be the complainant and the appeal is against acquittal, he is required to take leave as provided in Section 378 of the Criminal Procedure Code but if he is not the complainant, he is not required to apply for or obtain any leave. For the appeal against inadequacy of compensation or punishment on a lesser offence, no leave is necessary at the instance of a victim, whether he is the complainant or not.' 17. Kerala High Court has also in 'Omana Jose Vs. State of Kerala', ILR 2014 (2) Kerala 669 decided on 11.4.2014 on reference of Criminal Revision Petitions in the light of conflicting decisions in 'Sree Santosh Kumar vs M/S R R Constructions on 27 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174759889/ 6 Gokulam Chit and Finance Co. (P) Ltd. & Another Vs. T. Krishnakumar & Others', 2013 (4) KLT 547 (supra) and 'Shibu Joseph & Others Vs. Tomy K.J. & Others', ILR 2013 (4) Ker. 866, concluded: "For the aforesaid reasons, we hold that the complainant in a case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act cannot challenge the order of acquittal before the Sessions Court under the proviso to Section 372 of the CrPC and his remedy is only to file an appeal to the High Court with special leave under Section 378 (4) CrPC." 18.
